Hi Elena —

Thanks for flagging this early. Short answer: you can choose either behavior, but the default hosted behavior and enterprise controls differ. I'll summarize and attach our latest rate card and a short-runbook for procurement.

Options we support (hosted API):
1) Soft cap (recommended for self-serve)
   - We send tiered alerts (email + account webhooks) at X%, 90%, and 100% of the configured threshold.
   - Requests continue to be processed and are billed at normal per-token rates.

2) Hard cap / billing cutoff (good for regulatory/budget constraints)
   - When enabled, once the configured spend_limit is reached, further requests are rejected with a clear billing-exceeded error.
   - API behavior: requests return HTTP 402 with a JSON error {"code":"billing_exceeded","message":"Account spend limit reached"}.
   - No additional tokens are executed after the cap unless an override is issued by your billing contact or a contract amendment is signed.

3) Auto-throttle / degrade to lower-cost model (optional account-level policy)
   - For pilot/prod accounts we can configure automatic fallbacks: new requests are routed to a cheaper compatible model (e.g., from rdx-large -> rdx-medium) and/or we reduce max_tokens and sampling to conserve spend.
   - Throttled requests return HTTP 429 when they exceed per-second limits; the body will indicate "rate_limited" and include recommended retry-after.

Operational notes:
- Alerts: email + webhook + console banner. Webhooks include a billing_event payload (billing_threshold_percent, current_spend, threshold).
- Overages: if you do not enable a hard cap, overages are billed at the published per-token rate in the monthly invoice.
- Refunds/credits: handled case-by-case; small onboarding overages can be credited by finance with approval. Anything material requires a signed amendment.
- Emergency overrides: CS / Sales can enable a temporary lift (usually for <72 hours) after procurement email approval; it is tracked in the account audit log.

I'm attaching the rate card and a short procurement-facing FAQ. If you want a hard cap we can set it on your account today; you'll just need procurement to confirm the dollar amount and who can request an override.

Attachments: Redwood_rate_card_v3.pdf, sow-amendment-draft.docx

Let me know the cap amount and whether you want auto-fallback enabled.

Best,
Karthik
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Hi Elena — looping in a quick note from finance/sales ops perspective.

- SDKs: our official SDKs raise an exception and surface the billing_exceeded code when a 402 is returned. We also publish a short snippet for graceful handling in our integration docs; I'll paste that into the SOW appendix.
- Quality delta: the degrade-to-cheaper-model option is documented in the model catalog; we can provide sample prompts showing median latency and token-cost delta for the models you care about — we typically see 30-50% cost reduction with modest quality regressions for extraction tasks. We will add those artifacts to the SOW.
- Queuing: we do not queue user inference requests behind a billing cap. Requests are immediately rejected once the hard cap is hit. Throttling (429) can be used to slow traffic but is not a queue.
- Billing disputes: invoices are still issued during a dispute. For small onboarding issues we can apply a one-time credit; credit requests require approval and documentation from procurement.

If helpful, we can do a short procurement-only call to walk through the amendment language and the DocuSign flow. I can offer a one-time goodwill buffer (one month or $2,500, whichever is smaller) for pilots while we finalize the SOW — needs manager approval but usually straightforward for pilots.

Marissa
Head of Sales Operations
Redwood Inference
